newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe industrial index hits new all-time high.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe industrial index hits new all-time high.

text.p: Zimbabwean industrial shares continued their bull-run on Monday, powered to a record high by expectations of favourable growth prospects for the country's agriculture-led economy.
The key industrial index surged 131.37 points -- or 1.7 percent -- to break through the psychological 7,700-mark, ending at a new all time peak of 7,747.79.

"The market is very bullish and getting stronger with all the economic factors looking good. Economic growth forecasts are looking positive...interest rates are coming down which makes the stock exchange a more attractive home than the money market for investible funds." one broker said.
On current weather forecasts of near normal rains, Zimbabwe's economy is expected to grow by seven percent in 1997, up from five percent this year.

On the exchange on Monday, Zimbabwe's newly-listed hotel and supermarkets group Meikles leapt 400 cents to 2,000, blue-chip conglomerate Delta rose 100 cents to 3,400 while Alloys at 900 and furniture and clothing retailer Haddon and Sly at 300 each gained 50 cents.
Timber producer Border climbed 25 cents to 1,325, winery Cairns and tobacco firm TSL each gained 20 cents to 950 and 650 respectively.
Multi-industrial group Apex added 10 cents to 130 and five-cent gains were recorded in fencing supplier and clothing manufacturer CIH at 65, building group Mash at 160 and conglomerate TA at 165.

Minings were quiet with gold producer Ashanti rising 100 cents to 14,100 on what brokers said was a tentative move up as the bullion price moved uneasily in a tight band after coming off a steady price surge last week.
The mining index put on 7.18 points to end at 1,255.95.
